lead.headline: Human oversight needs evidence, not just a sign-off.
lead.summary: A UK Home Office survey exposes limits in users’ understanding of facial-search results, while Anthropic reports advances in automated safety testing. These are different evidence types: voluntary perceptions, developer evaluations and regulatory findings must not become unsupported claims of universal safety.

stories.title: A candidate match is not a final identification
stories.summary: The Home Office survey received 779 voluntary responses, representing 13% of eligible users. It found 34% misunderstood or were uncertain whether a facial-search match met a specified evidential standard. This is a finding about respondent understanding, not an algorithmic error or wrongful-arrest rate. Non-response limits generalisation. DΩP recommends testing comprehension before consequential decisions.

stories.title: Perceived efficiency is useful, but not a measured outcome
stories.summary: In the same voluntary survey, 88% of respondents perceived efficiency benefits. The survey does not independently measure time saved or final investigative accuracy. Assess benefits and burdens together: corroboration, investigation time, correction and remedy.

stories.title: Automated red teaming is a promising testing advance
stories.summary: Anthropic’s 12 November Anvil research reports stronger automated jailbreak discovery than expert human testers in studied biosecurity, cybersecurity and distillation tasks. These are developer-reported evaluations using internal frontier models with safeguards disabled, not independent field-safety validation. Defensive value depends on representative tests and verified remediation.

stories.title: Waymo inquiry examines whether the remedy worked
stories.summary: NHTSA opened RQ26006 on 6 November for 2,895 fifth-generation Waymo ADS vehicles. The regulator states that most reported incidents in its earlier evaluation occurred after the stated November 2025 remedy. The filing opens inquiry into adequacy and causes; it is not a final finding. No newer remedy outcome was verified in this recovery.

stories.title: Announced safeguards are not demonstrated protections
stories.summary: The 10 November Australian Government release proposes frontier-AI obligations and a regulator, including independent evaluation and rapid incident reporting. It describes future legislation, not evidence that protections are already operational. This recovery has not verified later legislative status. Implementation and practical recourse remain watchpoints.

outlook.label: Test the human control pathway
outlook.summary: DΩP proposes a versioned human-control evidence record: system and configuration, decision-maker, comprehension check, intervention result, correction route and affected people. This is an editorial proposal, not a validated standard.
outlook.quote: Human agency is prime. A person in the workflow is not proof of effective control.

report.title: The difference between formal oversight and demonstrated human control
report.standfirst: A scoped recovery of the missed Monday 16 November website edition, published 17 November after source rechecks. Original visual assets and the complete package remain unrecovered.
report.intro: We distinguish survey perceptions, developer research, policy proposals and regulator filings. Quantitative methodology remains unavailable; no scores, historical numerical trends or incident severity grades are assigned. The original inspectorate page was inaccessible, so detailed claims from it and the South Wales case are excluded from this recovery.

incidents.lesson: A deployed fix is not independent evidence that the hazard has stopped in representative conditions.

investigativeSummary: The recovery focuses on whether human review provides independent judgement. The Home Office’s voluntary facial-search survey found gaps in respondents’ understanding of an evidential threshold alongside perceived efficiency benefits. It cannot establish all-user error prevalence or causal enforcement outcomes. Affected people include those identified, investigators, victims and families. DΩP recommends a representative audit from candidate match through corroboration, enforcement, correction and remedy. The original inspectorate release was inaccessible; no claim here substitutes secondary reporting for a completed primary review. This is desk-based analysis, not original field reporting.
